sections.brief: What the mystery cults and philosophical schools taught about the soul: Eleusis epopteia and Cicero's 'better hope' (link ts13_mysteries), Samothrace open initiation and gradual fade, Orphic gold tablets, Pythagorean metempsychosis, Mithras' seven grades (Ostia Felicissimus mosaic vs Celsus's ladder via Origen 6.22), Isis (Apuleius XI), Plotinus (Porphyry, Life 23), Iamblichus' theurgy, Proclus. Figures: flow (Mithraic grades); compare (schools)

Closings by actor and document: CTh 16.10.10-12 (link vt21), Serapeum 391 (Theophilus under imperial order; Socrates V.16, Rufinus), Eleusis 392-396 (laws, then Alaric; Eunapius on the last hierophant), Hypatia March 415 (Socrates VII.15; Cyril's role disputed), Parthenon, Pantheon 609, San Clemente mithraeum, Justinian's Athens decree c.529 (Malalas; Watts, Cameron debate), Philae c.535-537 (Procopius; Dijkstra), Library of Alexandria myth graded (Bagnall). Figures: time (closings by actor)

Lost: the rites themselves, Porphyry's Against the Christians (burned 435, 448), the Athenian succession, fragments of Proclus; survived: Pseudo-Dionysius (Proclus-dependent, Eriugena 862, Rhineland mystics), Theology of Aristotle and Liber de causis via Arabic, Ficino's Pimander 1463 (link vt29, vt30); labelled interpretation (closing the rite, keeping the map) with counter-readings. Figures: compare (fate, actor, what remains)
